General rules when compiling this book1

NOTE 1

Contains 12 articles. (Author's note)

This book is divided into three volumes. The first book

collects ancient stories to arouse thoughts of preventing lust. The second book analyzes the arguments in detail, aiming to reveal and clearly present the methods and methods to prevent lust. The third book includes questions and answers, aimed at solidifying the basis of the prohibition against lust. Presented like this is to gradually go from shallow to deep, irreversible.

The cause and effect stories cited in this book

, along with the opinions and discussions of the ancients, are quoted from any book with clear footnotes, so that readers can verify. If we refer to other versions, we will point out discrepancies as a basis for comparison and clarification.

In the past, stories related to virginity and

Lust, most of it is easily spread by word of mouth everywhere, if it is considered that there is no clear evidence, then it is eliminated. For clear cause-and-effect stories in the present that no one has ever written down, collect them and add them.

The ancients recorded events often presented in

long way, continuously following each other without chaptering, making readers easily bored. In this book, the title is based on each incident, based on the title there is advice and encouragement, each

place is clear, helping readers easily distinguish and understand.

The stories included in the first book originate

from the works of many different authors, so the original has many differences in presentation, tone... Now when All included in this book have been edited and changed slightly for consistency.

Books that advise and prevent sexual immorality are

The ancients also wrote many works, but most of them only quoted ancient stories, taking them as reminders. As for people who really want to put in the effort to present specific and detailed methods, [applying them to everyday life situations like in this book], there has certainly never been one before.

The literature that promotes goodness and advises real life

is so abundant, at first glance it looks like a long river and a vast ocean, which is very gratifying. But if you examine it carefully, you will see that it only takes a few sentences to summarize the entire meaning. This book tries to overcome that limitation, so in the section "Methods of practice" (Book two), we try to use simple words but have a meaningful meaning. Although it only says to warn against lust, it also includes all the methods of behavior and practice in life. I hope that viewers will not be like riding a horse to look at flowers, it will be a waste of the editor's hard work.

The origin of lust lies in greed

craving. If the mind of craving has not been eliminated [then even if it is restrained

to control] is just like grass that has not been uprooted, but in the spring it will grow green again. Therefore, in volume two, in the contemplation of impurity and other contemplations, attention is paid to eliminating the mind right from the time when the mind of desire has not yet arisen. Only those who really practice can see the magic of this method. If you read it with a hasty mind, thinking that there is no connection to the basic intention, the person who composed this book would have no choice but to be like Ba Nha in the past [when he had not yet met Tu Ky, he could only] hold the piano and cry.

In the first two books, the method of preventing

lust is also complete, but just stating it and assuming it is true cannot help but raise doubts. Therefore, in the last book, one hundred questions and answers are raised, covering all issues in general.

The most important and essential issue for people

truly there is nothing more important than life and death, regardless of whether Confucianism or Buddhism is concerned. People today think that this is only a Buddhist issue, so they have long avoided mentioning it. This book aims to benefit all people, so why dare to shy away without mentioning it? Therefore, in both books two and three, regarding things such as the causes of life and death to theories about darkness, the author's limited knowledge is temporarily discussed and narrated.

All three books in this book are divided into

many sections, all of which have a clear order, from the first to the last. This is not only convenient for [readers in] adding and [taking notes on the content of each section], but also being able to extract each segment to record on small boards [hanging on seats, lying down or on the wall], to remind daily practice.

Writing a book for circulation in life is extremely difficult.

If you use crude words, it will not be suitable for intellectuals, but if you love elegance too much, it will not be suitable for the common people. For people with poor intelligence, even if they speak very clearly, they still have doubts, but for intellectuals, even if they only state the very essence, they will still be criticized as crude. Even if they are reincarnated saints, I am afraid it will be difficult to satisfy everyone's personal opinions, let alone post-graduates like us? In the sections on preventing sexual immorality in this book, there are things mentioned to help protect family happiness, there are things mentioned to help maintain good health, there are things mentioned to create happiness and eliminate disasters, there are things to cultivate the mind and nourish nature, and there are also things aimed at transcending life and death, escaping beyond the Three Realms. The mouth always talks about restraining sexual desire, but the thoughts of sexual desire in the heart become more and more intense. The cold river water seeped into the wound on his head and froze. He couldn't bear it anymore and died.

FORESTIONS

Being slashed in the head by a knife was so painful. Swimming across the glacier [in the middle of the night], it was so cold. The dead body was exposed naked, it was so embarrassing. Farewell to my wife and children, it's so tragic!

And all those things [pain, cold, shame, misery] were brought about by just one thought of adultery, causing them to suffer like that. Therefore, the Shurangama Sutra teaches: "When Bodhisattvas see lust, they should stay away from it like avoiding a pit of fire."

Truong Phu1

NOTE 1

Many people [in Thai Thuong] know this story. (Author's note)

In Thai Thuong district, there was a man named Truong Phu, who often raped women, even women

of good families were also raped by him. Later, he came to serve in the house of a high-ranking official in the district, relying on his power, so he became even more rebellious.

In the fall of the Dog year of the Kangxi era, the victims brought all of his evil deeds and denounced them to the [admiral commanding] the army. had to carry shackles and parade at Xuong Mon for all people to see, and at the same time sentenced him to life imprisonment and imprisonment until death.

DECLARATION

When I was at Xuong Mon, I personally saw this event, and returned just as the engraving book was not yet finished, so I had time to add this incident.

tieu_de: Advice to those who are addicted to green beans
noi_dung:
ADVICE TO THOSE who fall in love with the green roof1

NOTE 1

This section has two stories, setting two bad examples. (Author's note)

The widespread toxicity of prostitutes is truly terrifying! They cause other people's vitality to be exhausted, property to be lost, and husband and wife to be separated. Honest people are sincere, but being close to them becomes lustful; Intellectuals are wise, but being infatuated with them leads to confusion. [The place

green floor of] they always send people through the front door and pick up people at the back door, filled with so many filthy things. It's truly the most filthy place in the world, but how many worldly people are willing to go there, how strange! For homosexual men, the attachment is even more severe.

Fortunate to be born as a man, I cannot accept being humiliated by others. If you are in a position where you cannot accept being humiliated, but instead seek out the dirty path of prostitutes, wouldn't you bring trouble upon yourself? I don't know who started this bad custom [prostitution trading], but it still exists today. Those who are pure and noble must know how to stay away.

The two men Trieu and Luu1

NOTE 1

All over the capital, they told each other this story. (Author's note)

Trieu Lam is from Uyen Binh. Once he and Luu Phuong Vien went out to drink with a prostitute in a brothel, when suddenly her old lover, Vuong Tong Nghia, came to see her. [The two sides quarreled,] Luu Phuong Vien beat him and fell to death immediately.

The incident was reported to the district official. Liu Phuong Vien [bribed] a prostitute to falsely accuse Trieu Lam of killing the Vuong family. Trieu Lam must face death.

After that, one day Liu Phuong Vien was hosting a banquet for guests, a guest suddenly rushed forward and grabbed Liu Phuong Vien's hair, then made a voice similar to Trieu Lam's, saying: "The person you killed, you

are slandering me again. I have already denounced you to the underworld, both of you will be arrested."

Not long after that, Liu Phuong Vien and the other prostitute suddenly fell down and died.

DECLARATION

Duong Bang Nghe1 in the past never went to tea houses and liquor stores. Once a friend tricked him into taking him to a brothel. He returned home, burned all the clothes [he wore that day] and blamed himself severely. Compare this example with Trieu Lam and Liu Phuong Vien, how different is good and bad.

NOTE 1

Duong Bang Nghe: loyal mandarin of the Northern Song Dynasty, belonging to the faction that supported fighting the Jin invaders instead of making peace.

Truong Sung Nghia2

NOTE 2

This story was told by a friend of mine who witnessed it with his own eyes. (Author's note)

In the year of the Pig in the reign of Kangxi,3 in Vinh Ninh province, Son Tay province, there was a silversmith named Truong Sung Nghia, who had a homosexual affair with a stubborn and spoiled young maid named Vu Can Nhi Tu, neither eating nor sleeping apart.

NOTE LIKE 3

That means the year 1671.

One day, the Truong family got drunk and went to bed first. Vu Can Nhi Tu saw that Truong Sung Nghia was hiding a valuable thing, that night he killed him to take it and then fled. At that time, just after the fifth watch, Nhi Tu fled to the eastern city gate, but the city gate was still not open [so he could not escape

). In the morning, he was captured by the military and sentenced to immediate death.

FOR DECLARATION

Making a maid is a handsome and beautiful teenager in the house, often falling in love with women that turns into depravity. The Truong family's disaster was due to their attachment to appearance.

tieu_de: Advise people to repent of their mistakes
noi_dung:
ADVICE TO PEOPLE TO KNOW

REpenting of Mistakes1

NOTE 1

This section has three things, all mentioned good examples. (Author's note)

There are many adultery cases that people commit. Even though we don't see the evil retribution right in front of our eyes, in the dark and gloomy place, there are still people who secretly lose all blessings, some people who secretly have their lifespan stripped away, some people who are excluded from the path of academic success, and some people who die from poisonous snakes, tigers, leopards, or die by sword soldiers, because of being convicted at the mandarin's gate, or because of the tribulations of floods and droughts. If we ourselves can escape temporarily now, the retribution will also come to our children and grandchildren in the future; If this life does not pay for your sins, then in the next life you will have to pay in full. Just like a bird trapped in a net, no matter how much it struggles, it cannot escape. Like a fish in a leaky pot, the water dries out and is bound to die.

People in this world who move their hands and feet all fall into the hole

Deep underground, [full of dangers], yet still calm and fearless. Once the karma has come, the hands and feet are frantic, like a crab falling into a pan of boiling water. At that time, how can there be time to cry?

I would like to strongly advise everyone to soon clearly know [cause and effect of good and evil], be completely afraid of [bad and evil consequences], be completely ashamed of [unwholesome deeds], develop a strong mind towards Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and sincerely repent for each [wrong event]. In this way, the sins that arise from the [evil] mind will also be destroyed by the [sincere repentance] mind. If you do good deeds and accumulate virtue for long enough, [the sin hindrances] can be naturally [destroyed,] your body and mind will be as pure as before.

If you want to transcend the three realms,1 it is necessary to initiate the Bodhisattva vow, vowing in the future to save all sentient beings. For all sentient beings who suffer the retribution of the karma of lust, use the means of salvation, causing them to be reincarnated from the lotus flower. [in the Pure Land], not having to endure the prison of being in the mother's womb.

NOTE 1

Three realms (three realms): that is, the realm of Desire (Desire Realm), the Realm of Form (Form Realm) and the Formless Realm (Formless Realm). All sentient beings, depending on their karma, are born in samsara, and cannot go outside these three realms.

Developing such a mind will not only eliminate all evil karma, but will also receive immeasurable blessings. Therefore, in the Nirvana Sutra, it is taught: "For example, even if there is a thousand pounds of cotton, its value cannot be compared to just one pound of pure gold. Also, if a bowl of salt is poured into the Ganges River, the river water cannot taste salty at all." [For the Bodhi mind to save all sentient beings, no amount of karma can taint it.]

Let go of the butcher's knife and immediately regain an indestructible true body; Turn around and see the shore, immediately firmly on the edge of enlightenment. We must move forward quickly, because time passes and waits for no one. Whether wise or stupid, everyone should strive for themselves.

Hong Dao1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Dich Sand Luc. (Author's note)

During the Ming Dynasty, there was a man named Hong Dao, the second son of Duke Van Trung. One day, while he was going out of the latrine, he was dragged down to the underworld by the spirit of a dead servant. He saw a noble man wearing a silk shirt sitting in the middle, on both sides were two people wearing blue clothes standing as servants.

Hong Dao asked about the upcoming matter, the man in blue shirt immediately took out a book from his sleeve and showed it to him. Looking at it, he saw that the words were so tiny that it was hard to read. Hong Dao could see his name but could not read all the lines below. Finally, he read a note that said: "Should have been appointed as a political advisor, but on that day and month he committed adultery with a maid in the house, so he was demoted to Provincial Minister, to become Deputy Ambassador."

Hong Dao was scared and cried, the man in blue immediately said: "If you just try to do good, you can still redeem yourself."

Then Hong Dao came back to life, only to realize he had been dead for three days. Since then, I have been very diligent in doing good deeds. Later, he was indeed transferred to the Provincial Minister, as a Transport Ambassador for Mesopotamia. [Remembering the past,] he was extremely frightened, but in the end he was unharmed. He lived a long life and rose to the rank of Doan Minh Dien scholar.

COMMENT

The easiest way to commit adultery is to have sex with a maid, who knows that it will destroy your blessings? Therefore, we must be very careful in this matter.

Hang Mong Nguyen1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Tri Phi Tap. (Editor's note)

Hang Mong Nguyen is from Bac Truc, formerly known as Hang Duc Phan. One day, he dreamed that he should have passed the bachelor's degree in the Huong exam in the year of the Cat, but because he had an affair with two maids, his name was erased.

When he woke up, he swore from then on to keep the precepts of not committing adultery, and every year he engraved the Vajrayana sutra. Later, he dreamed that he went to a certain place and saw a piece of yellow paper with the name of the eighth passer, the surname Hang, written on it. In the middle was a word that could not be read clearly, and underneath he saw the word "integrity". Taking advantage of that dream, he changed his name to Hang Mong Nguyen.

In the year Nham Ty took the Huong exam, he passed twenty-ninth. In the year of the Goat, he took the Hoi exam and passed second. He was extremely skeptical [because it did not match his old dream]. When he took the exam, he passed the Second Rank and fifth, only to realize that when counting all three people who passed the First Rank1, he actually passed eighth, exactly as he saw in his dream. Later, he became an official to the position of Deputy Hien.2

NOTE 1

The first row is bordered by the top three winners: Poinsettia, Ban Lan and Tham Hoa. From the fourth person, ranks the Second Giap.

NOTE 2

Pho Hien: that is, the Vice Governor of Do Sat Vien.

COMMENT

Making an oath to keep the precepts from adultery is a very good thing. Engraving and printing the Sutras for circulation is even better. It's not just about getting rid of sins, [there will also be immeasurable blessings].

The Dien family3

NOTE 3

Excerpted from the book Impossible Unable to Record. (Author's note)

At the end of the Ming Dynasty, there was a man named Dien, who was rich and handsome, and many women courted him and wanted to get close to him. The Dien family knew in their hearts that it was wrong, but they couldn't keep it to themselves.

One day, he went to read a book at Nam Son pagoda, and a god appeared in broad daylight and said to him:

"Your family has great blessings, just because of amorous affairs, everything has been wasted. From now on, if you repent and correct your mistakes, you may be able to pass a doctorate, become an official or even a royal official. history.”

The Dien family from then on tried their best to practice and repent, and later on, they achieved what God said.

COMMENT

The book Essentials of Liberation teaches that: “If you want to repent of the lustful karma you have created, you should contemplate the [dangerous] female roots like the mouth of a poisonous snake, the old sins will naturally be destroyed.” A person who has committed the sin of lust cannot help but know this.

tieu_de: Advise people who have committed serious crimes
noi_dung:
ADVICE TO OFFENDERS

SERIOUS CRIMES1

NOTE 1

This section has three stories, all of which set bad examples must avoid. (Author's note)

The Avatamsaka Sutra teaches that: "The sin of adultery can cause sentient beings to fall into the three evil paths. [After leaving the three evil paths, if] one is born as a human, one must also suffer two types of retribution. One is that the wife cannot keep her virginity, and the other is that the relatives are not as desired." The Sutra of Sin and Blessing Retribution2 teaches that: "If you commit adultery with another person's wife, you will fall into hell and the cheating husband must

NOTE 2

That is, the Buddhist Sutra preaches the retribution of sin and blessings (佛說罪福報應經), 1 volume, translated by Mr. Cau-na-bat-da-la Chinese language, classified in the Mahayana Canon of Volume 17, sutra number 747.

hugging a copper column [burnt red], the annex is on an iron bed [burnt by fire underneath]. After leaving hell, one must be born in lowly lands and fall into the realms of chickens and ducks."

However, the above is only a general reference to the crime of adultery. If it is committed against one's close relatives, or monks and nuns who practice purity and commit adultery to defile them, then that is called a basic heinous sin. After death, one must fall into the Unintermittent Hell, continuously being cut, burned, crushed, cannot pause for a moment. Until this world has perished, one must be reborn in another world [to continue to suffer sins]. When another world is destroyed, one must be reborn in other worlds [to continue to suffer sins]. In the sutra, it is said in full about such things. If you have heard it, you cannot help but be frightened.

If there are people who, due to ignorance, have committed those serious crimes, or have not yet committed them but have such bad thoughts, they are also called criminals. You should know that such people, just waiting for three inches of breath to stop, will immediately fall into the Unintermittent Hell, for thousands of eons, and there is no limit to the desire to escape.

Those people should immediately take advantage of the time they still have a healthy life on earth, before the Three Jewels, earnestly and sincerely repent, make a vow to save all sentient beings, so that all can escape the three realms, then Only then can one attain Enlightenment.

If such a passionate and great aspiration can be generated, even though there is certain karma that must be endured, it will still be eliminated. Once upon a time, King Ajatasatru committed a great crime. Thanks to his earnest repentance, when he entered hell, he only had to suffer like a worldly prison for five hundred days.1 From this, it is enough to see that the merit of repentance is truly inconceivable. If we procrastinate and are lazy and refuse to make a determined effort, it will be difficult to avoid suffering for all eternity.

NOTE 1

This story is fully seen in the Sutra on the Bodhisattva's Conduct. (Author's Note) That is, the Buddhist sutra on the Bodhisattva's nature (佛說菩薩本行經), 3 volumes, is classified in the Mahazheng Pitaka, belonging to Volume 3, sutra number 155. This excerpt is located in volume 2, page 116, sheet c, starting from the 19th line.

Zhou dot exam2

NOTE 2

This story was told by a co-examiner with Mr. Chu, Ngo Ly Thanh. (Author's note)

The district official of Tu Tung was Chu Duy Cao. In the year of the Rooster under the reign of Khang Hy3, he was sent to Giang Nam to be an exam examiner. After he passed a candidate's exam, that night he dreamed that a demon appeared and said: "That person cannot pass." Saying that, he raised his hand and wrote out the word "lust". Chu Duy Cao did not understand and asked, the ghost replied: "That person had adultery with his stepmother's daughter, for that he was punished by heaven."

NOTE 3

That is the year 1669.

The next day, Chu Duy Cao forgot what happened in the dream and still brought the exam to present. The examiner highly praised the article, then crossed out the two words "dangerous". Seeing this, Chu Duy Cao immediately said: "In the exam papers of the candidates in this round, many people use those two words, perhaps they should not be deleted." The examiner listened and changed his mind, ordering Chu Duy Cao to erase the crossed out spot. When it was time to erase, he suddenly saw that the ink had penetrated several layers of paper. Chu Duy Cao suddenly remembered the dream he had last night and immediately decided to fail the exam.

COMMENT

People in Northern Cau-lo, when men and women want to be close to each other, they go together under the same tree. At that time, the tree canopy on all four sides immediately lowered to cover them, and then inside there were naturally enough beds and pillows. If that woman is the man's mother, aunt or sister, the tree canopy will definitely not cover it. If you try to force yourself to commit adultery, the tree will die.1

NOTE 1

See in the Sutra of the Origin of Humanity. (Author's note)

From this, it can be seen that fornication with a blood relative is taboo against the religion of heaven. Just failing the exam2 is not enough to punish that sin!

NOTE 2

The original work used “expulsion from Ton mountain - 擯出孙山” (kicked out of Ton mountain) to refer to failing the candidate. This example comes from a saying in the collection Qua Dinh Luc (过庭录) by Pham Cong Xuu (1126-1158) in the Southern Song Dynasty. People of later generations also often say "Ton Son's name is lost" or "Ton Son's son is a foreigner", both of which refer to people who fail the exam.

Hua Trieu Hinh1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Induction of Heavenly Theory. (Author's note)

Hua Trieu Hinh is a native of Tan Giang, passed the bachelor's exam in the year Mau Ngo, and set out to Phuc Ninh to pay his respects to the examiner of the exam. When he happened to pass by a small hermitage, he saw a young nun he liked. He teased her, but the nun refused, so he used force to rape him.

The next day, Trieu Hinh suddenly went crazy, bit off his tongue and died.

COMMENT

That was just nothing. is the leopard2 present, while the real retribution awaits in hell.

NOTE 2

Flowers: evil retributions must be suffered immediately, such as a tree blooming and then bearing fruit. Evil deeds must attract the present retribution called flowers, just like a flowering tree, then the right conditions must meet the real retribution, just like a tree with enough time to bear the fruit.

The person on the boat offering incense3

NOTE 3

This story told by a person in Suzhou who went to offer incense together. (Author's note)

In the first year of the Thuan Tri era,4 there was a couple who went by boat to offer incense at Cuu Hoa mountain, and slept on the boat at night. There was a bad guy who saw that his wife was beautiful, so around midnight he disguised himself as a husband and went to have sex with her. The wife found out early in the morning and was so embarrassed that she hanged herself and died. The husband was extremely miserable, bought a temporary coffin

NOTE 4

That was the year 1644.

his wife's body was on the side of the road, waited to go up the mountain to complete the incense offering ceremony and then immediately brought the coffin back to his hometown.

When I got home, I suddenly saw my wife already there. The husband was frightened and thought he was seeing a ghost, but the wife said, "You were the one who brought me back before." The husband became even more frightened, immediately opened the coffin lid to see, it turned out that inside was the person who was on the same boat [who did bad things the other night], on the neck there was a mark like a hanged person.

This thrilling story spread far and wide, so the people who came to Cuu Hoa mountain to offer incense became more and more respectful and numerous.

DECLARATION

The person who offers incense must be a good man and woman, that's why the retribution comes to that person so miraculously and quickly.

tieu_de: Advise people to develop their mind to go beyond the world
noi_dung:
ADVICE TO THOSE WHO GIVE THE MIND

Exodus1

NOTE 1

This section quotes the ten stories of the sutra, citing eight good examples and two good examples. bad. (Author's note)

During the Buddha's time, one day at Ky Vien monastery, four monks discussed together what was the most miserable thing in this world. One thinks it is the most painful lust, one thinks it is hunger and thirst, another thinks it is anger, and the last one thinks it is terror and fear. The four argued endlessly. Therefore, the Buddha taught: "What you have raised to argue is not the meaning of saving suffering. Suffering in this world is nothing more than possessing the body. Things such as hunger, thirst, lust, anger, resentment, all arise from this body. Therefore, the body is the root of all suffering, the source of all disasters and tribulations."1

NOTE 1

Excerpt from the Dhammapada. (Author's note) Actually, this content is quoted from the Dhammapada Sutra (法句譬喻經), a total of 4 volumes, classified in the Mahazheng Pitaka, belonging to Volume 4, sutra number 211. The quoted part is in volume 3, page 595, sheet a, starting from the 13th line.

In particular regarding lust, having a female body You will naturally fall in love with men; if you have a male body, you will naturally fall in love with women. Reputation is ruined, integrity is destroyed, blessings are lost, life expectancy is reduced, all are due to that. For example, if you maintain purity and virtue, you will surely enjoy wealth thanks to that. But when you enjoy wealth, it is very easy to create bad karma. Just one day of doing evil will result in retribution for thousands of lifetimes, so what you gain cannot make up for what you lose. For example, when enjoying happiness, you still diligently practice good karma, you will definitely be born in heaven. But once the heavenly blessings have ended, they must return to reincarnation. Therefore, in the sutra it is said: "The Holy King of Chakravarti rules over all four continents of the world. He can fly freely in the sky, but when he runs out of blessings, he is reborn as a small insect living on the neck of a buffalo."

So know that, even if it is karma and blessings, everything will eventually become the cause of

fall, whether it is hell or heaven, all will not escape samsara. If you do not strongly develop the mind to go beyond the world, single-mindedly follow the path of enlightenment, only in vain do trivial and trivial things, doing good today, doing evil tomorrow, struggling forever in the three evil paths, unable to escape the eight troubles, 1 is really not the direction of a man.

NOTE 1

Eight difficulties: Eight very difficult situations for practicing according to Buddhism.

However, the noble music is rarely followed by anyone, these words can only be said to those with superior wisdom.

Buddha's birthday student2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Shakyamuni Tathagata's spectrum (釋迦如來譜). This part seems to have nothing to do with the prevention of lust, but because we want to open up the story for the next part, we cannot help but clearly state the reason for the Buddha's birth, and also to ensure that a passage about this great cause and condition is not lost. (Author's note)

The original Buddha Shakyamuni attained enlightenment countless eons ago. Because he wanted to save sentient beings, he split into countless incarnations and appeared in different worlds. Taking only the reincarnation event of Shakyamuni [born] in this world, it is the crown prince [Siddhartha] son of King Tinh Phan in Thien Truc country.3 Before being born, he lived in Tusita heaven, named Bodhisattva Thien Tue.

NOTE 3

Thien Tue Bamboo: a name the Chinese use to call India.

At that time, the country of Thien Truc had a holy king, King Tinh Phan, and a holy queen, his wife Ma-da, both of whom were ancient Buddhas of the past, embodied as kings and mother of the country. The Bodhisattva rode a white elephant with six tusks, descended from the sky, and entered the right hip of the holy mother. After that, she immediately felt her body was happy and relaxed, as if she were drinking nectar, and her wisdom and eloquence also naturally appeared. The magical dishes of the heavenly gods also naturally appeared to her in full.

When it was time to give birth, the holy mother and her maid strolled in the garden, coincidentally raising her right hand to hold on to the ba-la-xoa flower branch.1 At that moment, the crown prince was born from the right hip of the holy mother, radiating a bright light throughout heaven and earth, thousands of saints appeared at the same time, joyfully praising. From the ground suddenly emerged two lakes of fragrant water, one cold water lake, one hot water lake, to bathe the prince's body. In the air, nine dragons appeared again spraying water, four heavenly kings appeared together carrying the crown prince, and the heavenly king Dao Loi covered him in heavenly clothes.

NOTE 1

That is, the flower has no worries.

At that time, the prince immediately turned to all directions, each direction took seven steps, saying: "In heaven and under heaven, only I am the most noble."

At that time, King Tinh Phan was sitting on the palace hall with his ministers discussing matters of state, when suddenly he heard a minister playing a joyful drum, announcing the ecological birth.

word. Everyone wanted to take the precious carriage [of the holy mother and the crown prince] back to the palace. The angel Ty-shy-ma immediately appeared in a carriage with seven treasures, with four heavenly kings as the charioteers. The gods of heaven all appeared down in the middle of nowhere, burning magical and magical incense to make offerings to the prince.

The prince was born with thirty-two good signs and eighty beauties. At the age of nineteen, he became a monk and attained enlightenment at the age of thirty. That's just the most brief things to say, for detailed details, please see the sutras in the Tripitaka. It's not possible to say everything here.

NO INFECTION WITH THE BEARING CHARACTERS1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Sutra of Buddha's Nature of Conduct (彿本行經) and the Sutra of Past Cause and Effect (過去因果經). (Author's note)

At that time, King Tinh Phan brought all the gifts to marry Princess Da-du-da-la as crown prince, along with two other concubines named Cu-di and Loc-da. Thus, the crown prince has three concubines.2

NOTE 2

We found this excerpt in its entirety in the book Shakyamuni Tathagata Yinghua Luc (釋迦如來應化錄) compiled by Bao Thanh in the Ming Dynasty, included in the Treasury of Thousand Continues, Volume 75, Sutra number 1511. This excerpt is on page 63, sheet b, starting from the 23rd line, bearing the title of the paragraph as Siddhartha Phi (悉達納妃). This paragraph opens with the sentence “Cause and effect are the clouds” (因果經云). This proves that the An Si Sutra was quoted from this book and relied on the opening sentence to quote, not from the Sutra of Karma as noted above. However, about the second crown prince named Cù-di, in the book Śākyamuni Buddha (the same book that the An Si Complete Book in the previous paragraph called Sakyamuni Buddha), there is this passage: “太子年十七。王為納妃簡選數千。最後一 女名曰裘夷端正第一 禮義備 舉。是則 宿命賣花女也。” - The crown prince is in his 10th year, the crown prince accepts the concubine, shortens the year book. In the end, the most famous female author wrote Cu-di, decency is the first, and propriety is recommended. Thi Tac Tuc lives forever with wild flowers. “(The crown prince was seventeen years old. The king wanted to recruit a crown prince. He searched for many years. Finally, he found a girl named Cu-di, beautiful and dignified like no one else, and full of manners and virtue.This is the girl selling flowers [who had an affinity with the crown prince] in her past life.) (Mahayana Tripitaka, Volume 50, Sutra No. 2040, page 6, sheet c, starting from line 3) According to such a description combined with the story of the previous life selling lotus flowers, it can be certain that this book is referring to Princess Da-du-da-la, but for some reason, the name Cu-di is used (this same book, in another passage, it says Cu-di裘夷 / 瞿夷). Through this, we have some doubts about the crown prince having 3 wives. Firstly, this matter is not mentioned in any other scriptures, only in the book Sakyamuni Tathagata Yinghua Luc it is mentioned, but the annotation is not accurate. Second, comparing with Śākyamuni Buddha, we see that this book shows signs of confusion if Da-du-da-la and Cu-di are actually just one person. Third, Ms. Loc-da's name is not mentioned in any other scriptures, so based on the previous two questions, the fact that the book Sakyamuni Tathagata-li-hāgata mentioned this name is not reliable enough.

The king ordered three palaces to be built, with three thousand serving maids. The maids of the first palace take care of serving the prince from early in the day, the second palace serves from midnight, and the third palace serves from after midnight to morning. Thousands of melodious songs were always played in the palace, day and night without end.

The Crown Prince often walked, stood, and sat with his concubines, but absolutely no worldly thoughts arose. In the quiet night, he only specialized in practicing meditation, never doing anything like husband and wife with his concubines.

The Bodhisattva of Demons1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Samadhi Sea Sutra. (觀彿三昧海經). (Author's note)

When the prince came to sit under the Bodhi tree to meditate, Demon King Ba-Tuan saw that the prince practiced vigorously and wanted to destroy his virtue. He gathered all the heavenly demons, poisonous dragons, and demons, and dragged them to the place where the prince was practicing. Question:The scriptures mention the intermediate state, what is it referring to?

Answer: That is only for consciousness. As the Nirvana Sutra2 teaches, the general idea is summarized as follows: At the time of death, family and relatives surround and mourn, the dying person is frightened and frightened, unable to control himself. At that time, all the good and bad things you have done throughout your life appear before your eyes. After the warm air in the body disappears, the five aggregates of the past disappear and the present intermediate body arises. After entering the womb, the present intermediate body disappears, and the five aggregates of the future are born. Just like when a light is turned on, darkness disappears. When the light is turned off, darkness arises, continuously changing, without interruption.

NOTE 2

Sravakas [reborn] after leaving the womb still forget all the past, Bodhisattvas still have the illusion of reincarnating from one life to another, let alone ordinary people?

Question: At the moment of death, if thoughts of desire arise, one must fall. However, [in this book, in the Samsara Contemplation section, it is said that] sentient beings in Cu-dani, when entering the intermediate state, saw the goddess and hugged them, and were immediately born in heaven. How could that be?

Answer: Mindfulness at the time of death is indeed extremely important. However, the merit to be born in heaven is inherently created by sentient beings throughout their lives. For example, if the tree trunk leans completely towards the east, then when cutting down the root, it must fall towards the east. If it leans towards the west, then when cutting down the root, it must fall towards the west.

Question: In the Contemplation Sutra, the nine chapters of rebirth in the Pure Land are described, all of which see the appearance of a lotus flower. [In this book, it is said] sentient beings in the Uat-dan-viet continent who are born in the heaven of the middle class also see the appearance of lotus flowers, so how can they differentiate?

Answer: Sutras teach that, [in the nine chapters of rebirth,] in each chapter there is an Incarnate Buddha appearing to lead the person to be reborn. As for people born in heaven, of course they cannot see the Buddha.

Question: [In this book it is said that] if people are reborn in the womb of dogs or pigs, they will see beautiful women. Sentient beings in Cu-da-ni are born in heaven and also see beautiful women, so how can they differentiate?

Answer: [Even though they look the same,] one side

belongs to sex, the other side belongs to the mind. The mind is light and pure, so it is born in heaven; Sexual desire is rough and heavy, so it must fall. As it is taught in the Shurangama Sutra: “[A person who is about to die is judged by the two parts of his mind: emotions and thoughts.] If he is completely composed of thoughts, he will gently fly up and be born in heaven. If he has the blessing of wisdom along with pure vows, his mind will naturally open and he will be reborn in the Buddha realm.

“If emotions are few and thoughts are many, he will be born as a flying fairy, a demon king, or a yaksha with the ability to fly.

“If love and thoughts are equal, they will not rise to a higher level, nor will they fall to a lower level, they will immediately be reborn in the human world. In the human world, if you have many good thoughts, you will be intelligent and bright, if you have many thoughts of desire, you will be dull.

“If your feelings are too much, your thoughts will be low, you will fall into the animal world. Among animals, if the evil karma is heavy, then one is born as an animal on land; if the evil karma is lighter, one is born as a bird.

“If there are up to seven parts of emotion, three parts of perception, one must fall into the aquatic life, or be born as a hungry ghost.

“If there are nine parts of emotion and only one part of perception, one must fall into hell. If you commit a light crime, you will go to hell, and there will be a temporary reprieve; If you commit a serious crime, you will enter the endless hell, and you will have to endure suffering without any pause.

"If it is purely emotion without thought, you will fall into Avici hell."

Question: People who fall into Avici hell, as soon as they enter, immediately encounter eighty-four thousand forests of swords and swords, but they look like forests of precious trees; encountering a hot volcano, but seeing it like a lotus flower; I met iron-beaked birds, but I saw them as gentle swallows. People born in heaven also see similar scenes, how can they differentiate?

Answer: People who fall into hell, at the time of death, are burned by the fire of karma, so false thoughts arise. Because of that delusion, false views become. As for people born in heaven, the four elements are quick and light. When it's hot, a cool wind blows, and when it's cold, a warm air rushes up, so they can't be considered the same.

tieu_de: Explain clearly the wonderful nature of nature
noi_dung:
EXPLAINING THE MIRACULOUS

OF THE NATURE1

NOTE 1

This section has 7 questions and answers. (Author's note)

Question: Quy Lo asked about life and death, Trong Ni2 refused to talk.3 As for him, he kept talking endlessly [about life and death], not just searching

NOTE 2

Trong Ni: that is, Confucius.

NOTE 3

Excerpted from the book Analects, chapter Advancement, section 11. Original text: “季路問事鬼神？子曰：未能事人，焉能事鬼？曰：敢問 死？曰：未知生，焉知死？- Quy Lo questioned the ghost and god Tu wrote: Write: Thank you for your life, your peace for your death? (Qui Lo asked about worshiping ghosts and gods. Confucius replied: If you cannot serve humans, how can you serve ghosts and gods? Again: Dare to ask about death? Answer: Not knowing about life, how can you know about death?)

useless things that make people behave strangely?

Answer: Actually, Confucius replied: "If you don't know about life, how can you know about death?" That is the Gentleman's way of leading and opening, not avoiding and refusing to answer. Confucius also said: "Life and death are also big matters."1 So, how can we say that discussing life and death is useless and different from life?

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Zhuangzi. (Author's note)

Question: Is that what Buddhism calls essence, the theory of "no good, no evil"?

Answer: If you think that there is no good, no evil, then you fall into the void of confusion, that is, the theory of cessation. If people in this world are not attached to existence, they will certainly be attached to emptiness; If you are not attached to both existence and non-existence, you will certainly be attached to non-existence and non-existence. Therefore, the Samadhi Sutra compares this [limited understanding] to blind people touching an elephant.

People who are blind from birth have never seen an elephant. There was a king who called a number of such blind people and asked: "Do you want to know the shape of an elephant?" The blind people said they wanted to know. The king immediately ordered the mahout to lead an elephant to the front yard, then told the blind men to come and touch the elephant. Then, the king asked: "Do you now know the shape of an elephant?" Everyone said they knew. [The king immediately asked them to describe it.]

The person who touched the elephant's ear said, "The elephant is [round, thin] like a sieve." The person touching the elephant's nose said: "The elephant [big head and small head] is like a guitar." The person who touched the ivory said, “The elephant [is round and long] like a wooden stake.” The person touching the elephant's back said: "The elephant is like a house." The person touching the elephant's side said, "The elephant is like a wall." The person touching the elephant's tail said, "The elephant is like a big broom." The person touching the elephant's foot said: "The elephant is like a pillar."

Those blind people, everyone thought they were right, tried their best to argue with others. They argued endlessly, until finally they broke into a fight. The king immediately laughed and said: "You all don't know the shape of an elephant. Some say a sieve, that's an elephant's ear; some say a guitar, that's an elephant's nose; some say a stake, that's an elephant's tusks; some say a house, that's an elephant's back; some say a wall, that's an elephant's ribs; some say a broom, that's an elephant's tail; some say a pillar, that's an elephant's foot."

The blind people who heard the king didn't dare to argue, but in their hearts they still believed that What I know is correct and not wrong. People [when they are not yet enlightened] talk about nature, it's just the same.

Question: All things, if they are created, they will be destroyed, if they have a beginning, they will have an end. So, does the physical nature have birth and destruction?

Answer: Normally, everything that has form must have formation, destruction, birth, and destruction. But nature is inherently formless, so how can there be birth and death?

Question: So, is the essence the same as emptiness?

Answer: It's not like that. The emptiness of nothingness is a confused emptiness, without awareness. The emptiness of the nature is called emptiness, what is not real.

Question: The ears and eyes are part of form, the ability to hear and see is part of consciousness. If consciousness is truly not destroyed, the ability to hear from childhood to adulthood must be the same. However, when people get old, their eyes become dull and their ears become deaf, so the nature of seeing and hearing also has aging and death. Accordingly, when considering, we know that consciousness also has birth and death.

Answer: Ignoring eyes and deaf ears are all caused by [weakness] of the body, what does it have to do with the nature of seeing and hearing? The seeing eye does not have the ability to see on its own, but must rely on the nature of seeing to be able to see; The ear that hears sound does not have to be able to hear on its own, but must rely on the nature of hearing to be able to hear. If it is thought that the eye can see on its own, then the dead person can still see with his eyes open, and when dreaming, the eyes are closed, so it should not be possible to see all the images [in the dream.] If it is thought that the ear can hear on its own, then the dead person can listen with his ears up, and when dreaming with his body in bed, he should not be able to hear the sounds [in the dream] in other distant places. In this way, how can [the nature of seeing, the nature of hearing] have birth and death?

Question: Saying that nature has no birth and death, I have temporarily understood, but saying that nature has no coming or going, I really don't understand.

Answer: [If you see that there are dharmas] that suddenly come and go, those are all due to the mind's delusions, not their true nature. The vast true nature covers the whole of space, even the great world within our nature is just like a bubble floating on the surface of the vast ocean.

Question: The retribution in the three evil paths, up to being reborn in the human world, if discussing about form is decided by the King of Hell, but if discussing about nature, it is all influenced by each person's own created karma. Please ask, so which is right and which is wrong?

Answer: If there is no attachment, then both theories are correct, but if there is attachment, both theories are wrong. For example, if a husband and wife give birth to a child, if both are heartless, even if each person says that it is the child I gave birth to, it will not cause any harm. But if two people get angry and compete with each other, each person believes that the child was born to him or her, not to the other person, then both people are wrong.

tieu_de: The cause of falling into evil paths
noi_dung:
CAUSES OF FALLING IN

EVIL ROADS 1

NOTE 1

This section has 10 questions and answers. (Author's note)

Question: Birds such as lovebirds, pigeons, etc., have created sexual karma in previous lives, so in this life they are born as birds [also heavy with sexual karma],

but once the swallow loses its mate, even when it dies, it will not look for another. It can be clearly seen that in its previous life it did not create adultery, so why must it fall? into birds?

Answer: Adultery is only one of the ten evil karma. All ten of these karma can lead to falling as animals. Like the lovebirds, the robins, and the pigeons [all of whom are heavily lustful], they all fall into animals due to adultery, but the swallow's karma may be due to other evil things. In the Cau-xa commentary, it is said: "Just as people who create bad karma must fall into the animal world, each person is different. In general, if lust is heavy, he will be reborn as pigeons, sparrows, lovebirds..., if anger is heavy, he will be reborn as snakes, centipedes, scorpions..., if he is too ignorant, he will be reborn as goats, pigs, clams, oysters..., if he is too arrogant, he will be reborn as goats, pigs, clams, oysters... tigers, wolves, lions..., if they are often busy making fun of them, they will be reborn as monkeys. If they are too greedy and jealous, they will be reborn as hungry dogs.

Question: People who create bad karma must fall into the animal world. At that time, will they know whether they are animals or not?

Answer: At that time, they cannot control themselves. okay.

Question: Why can't you control yourself after death?

Answer: Actually, while you're alive, can you ever control yourself? The same beautiful woman, when a lustful

person sees it, he is filled with endless love and attachment, a jealous woman sees it and hates it to the bone. Now that he has [been manipulated like that by the external environment,] let alone after death?

Question: Once upon a time, there was a Heavenly King of the Dao-loi heaven. Knowing that his lifespan was about to end, [according to karma] he was about to fall into the form of a donkey, he wholeheartedly took refuge in the Three Jewels. [Afterwards, when he entered the womb of a donkey and donkey mother] he immediately had a miscarriage, and at that moment was reborn again as a God. king.1 How should this story be explained?

NOTE 1

This story is told in the Dhammapada sutra. (Author's note)

Answer: He had extremely profound blessings in his previous life, so he could change back to become the Heavenly King of heaven. Otherwise, [at the time of conception,] even though the mother donkey is in front of your eyes, you only see it as a beautiful woman, even though the smell of filth in the stable rises, you still smell like the scent of a sandalwood, [and immediately develop a liking for it.]

Question: The number of people in life is very large, life's affairs are extremely complex and complex, if each event was recorded in detail, even a mountain of ink would not be enough. Why did the King of Hell have to spend so much time worrying about and recording these things?

Answer: All dharmas are created by the mind. The mind can create heavenly palaces, but it can also create hellscapes. Inside the heavenly palace there are many beautiful scenes, but they are not entirely due to construction. People who are reborn in heaven naturally have everything to enjoy.

In hell there are countless detailed structures, which are not created by construction. People who fall into it naturally have everything and then have to suffer.

Question: While alive, all the pain and suffering were borne by this body. After death, without a body, who will suffer?

Answer: Pain and suffering are in the mind, not in the body. If pain is in the body, then the dead should also know pain.

Question: People who create bad karma must of course suffer heavy crimes, but those good hells and demon kings also torture people extremely cruelly, so in what hell do they have to suffer retribution?

Answer: If it is based on facts, good hells [in the world] obey the orders of [gods]. government] beating someone, certainly cannot be charged with beating someone again. According to logic, all the good hells and demon kings in hell also appear from the minds of sinners.

Question: If hell is a real realm, it should be made visible to all people, so they can believe.

Answer: There are people everywhere who have seen hell, but unfortunately those who have seen it cannot return [to tell it again].

Question: The Tathagata used one of his toes to press the ground, and the entire world immediately turned into a solemn pure gold color. This story is told in the

Vimalakirti Sutra. With such supernatural power, why doesn't he destroy all the hells in the ten directions, helping sentient beings who are suffering in hell to be reborn in the Buddha realm?

Answer: Even the great physician king cannot cure diseases that are certain to lead to death, nor can he cure those who refuse to take medicine. Those who create bad karma are themselves subjected to suffering and retribution. Bodhisattvas cannot save them and exempt them from sin. Just like the poor have no blessings, the rich cannot eat and drink for them to make them full.

Question: If such certain karma cannot be avoided, then Buddha's teachings cannot change anything. But in the Sutras it is always said to "save countless sentient beings", what does that mean?

Answer: All the sufferings of the world are caused by bad karma. Advising people not to create evil karma to completely eliminate all suffering, isn't that salvation?

tieu_de: Reasons for establishing the wedding ceremony
noi_dung:
SETTING CAUSE

WEDDING CEREMONY1

NOTE 1

This section has 8 questions and answers. (Author's note)

Question: If sexual immorality is at the top of all evil things, the Holy Kings of ancient times when ruling should have completely stopped it, but King Phuc

Hy invented matchmaking to connect the two sides, forming a marriage, so what?

Answer: That is because we want to stop the lust [chaos] in the world. If we don't establish marriage rituals, men and women all over the world, regardless of who they are, can do lewd things with each other, just like animals, and when they give birth to children, they will definitely abandon them and not raise them. Therefore, it is necessary to devise means and establish the rituals and rules of marriage, so that throughout the world, every man can only live as husband and wife with his wife, women can only live as husband and wife with their husband, and parents are responsible for raising their children, and all must follow the same rules so as not to be chaotic.

Question: Why do we give the right to marry men and women to the matchmaker?

Answer: Through matchmaking, it is because we fear that there will be cunning and deceitful people who want to marry beautiful people but disparage ugly people, creating competition between each other.

Question: Why must many ceremonies be established? doubts such as asking for names, asking for sand, asking for permission...?

Answer: Because I'm afraid that in the future there will be unruly people who can easily mix with each other, so we have to lay out such clear rituals [to force them to follow].

Question: I now know the original reason for establishing the marriage ritual, but I don't know when the relationship between men and women originally originated?

Answer: According to the Human Origin Sutra1, when the world was first established, all sentient beings were reincarnated from the Light and Sound heaven, naturally reincarnated, not born from the mother's womb. [At that time, the ground in this realm produces substances that taste as sweet as honey, and living beings eat them naturally and are full of energy.] But over a long period of time, they greedily eat those foods, and imagine that the bodies of living beings gradually change to become ugly, giving birth to tendons, veins, bones, marrow... and begin to divide into different male and female forms, and then sex arises. That is the initial origin of the relationship between men and women.

NOTE 1

The Sutra of the Beginning of the Human World (起世因本經), a total of 10 volumes, translated into Chinese by Bodhisattva Dharma, is classified in the Mahazheng Pitaka of Volume 1, sutra number 25.

Question: Confucianists believe that there are three sins of filial piety, of which not giving birth to descendants is the greatest sin. The Buddha taught people to leave their families and become monks to practice Buddhism, and furthermore clearly pointed out the dangers in secular life. Why are Confucianism and Buddhism so different?

Answer: [From a worldly perspective,] the good work of Confucianism and Buddhism is different, but both sides also aim to help society be peaceful and prosperous. People have different temperaments, there are places where Buddhism cannot be taught but Confucianism can be taught, and there are places where Confucianism cannot be taught but Buddhism can be taught

chemistry. Therefore, the saints of the Three Religions, 1, although united in their efforts to [educate people], cannot help but divide into different aspects. Each religion has established its own sect and has its own method of education. Although the name is divided into three, it is actually just one.

NOTE 1

Three religions: refers to Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism.

For example, three doctors all want to cure diseases and save people, but people's illnesses are inherently different. If all three learn the same method, the treatment will not be widespread. For example, when encountering a fire disaster, there are three rich men who all want to save the people from the city. If all three open the same city gate, they cannot save many people.

So, if you can follow Confucius' teachings to the best of your ability, Śākyamuni Buddha will certainly be happy to see it. If he could do his best to follow Shakyamuni's teachings, Confucius would certainly be happy to see it. If we think that we must follow our religion to be good, then we will be satisfied; If I don't follow my religion and it's good, I'm still not satisfied, then I can't be a Buddha or a saint.

During the Sui Dynasty, Ly Si Khiem once said: "The three religions are like the light of the sun, the moon and the stars, one of which cannot be missing."2 People of later generations argue endlessly about this, only revealing their own narrow-mindedness. That's it.

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Sui Shu. (Author's note)

Question: Some people say that saints like Phuc Hy, Emperor... are all great Bodhisattvas who appear in incarnation, I wonder if that is true?

Answer: That is also possible. If a family is good at making bows, their children will first let their children learn how to make all kinds of winnows and winnows... If a family is good at metal casting, their children will first learn how to make wool coats.3 In Buddhism, there is a dharma of transformation, there is an authentic dharma, there is a dharma of gradual practice, there is a dharma of cutting down. Abandoning sexual desire and becoming a monk to practice the Dharma is an authentic and profound Dharma. Getting married, practicing at home, that is the transformation of the law, gradual practice. If there is a person who cannot be a vegetarian, we should first advise them to use three types of clean meat.4 The saints of the Three Teachings all have the same mind, the same principle.

NOTE 3

This sentence is taken from the book of Rituals and Thien Hoc Ky, implying that although things are different, they have similarities, such as learning to make saws and sieves and being good at bending bamboo. Only then can the arc be made.

NOTE 4

Three types of pure meat (Three pure flesh): That is the meat of the animal that: 1. My eyes do not see that the animal was killed for me. 2. The ear does not listen to a trustworthy person saying that the animal was killed because of him. 3. There is no reason to suspect that that animal was killed because of him.

Question: If everyone in humanity stopped having sex, then after a hundred years there would be no more humans, so what would happen?

Answer: In this impure world, boys and girls who have not yet had time to get married will be married before they reach the age of twenty. Secretly looking at each other, ready to follow each other, how could anyone stop having sex? As long as you look at yourself, you're afraid you haven't been able to do the same, let alone other

people? Like a fisherman who doesn't catch fish on a day off, but is worried that [the river is full of fish] and the boat won't be able to navigate, it's no different than people from the Ky country worrying about the sky collapsing.1

NOTE 1

Once upon a time, there were people from the Ky country who stopped eating and sleeping because they were worried that the sky might fall. The following person used this quote to refer to people who worry about nothing, similar to the proverb we have: "Worrying about cows with white teeth."

Question: Even though you say that, what if that really happened?

Answer: If that were the case, then all over this world would be like reincarnated gods, no longer having to be born from the prison of a fetus.

questions about repentance

AND RENAISSANCE2

NOTE 2

This section has 7 questions and answers. (Author's note)

Question: If you have accidentally created the karma of lust, should you repent in front of the Buddha's altar, or should you rely on your own mind to repent?

Answer: The mind is the Buddha, the Buddha is the mind. Repenting in front of the Buddha altar does not prevent you from repenting based on your own mind; Repenting based on your own mind does not prevent you from repenting before the Buddha altar. [It is not necessary to choose one of the two?]

Question: The lustful karma created in this life, of course, needs to be repented to eliminate. But with the lustful karma created in the past [previous life], it is obscure and cannot be remembered, so what is the need to repent?

Answer: All of us from countless lifetimes past until today, no matter how we were born in the four ways of birth,1 no matter where we were born in the six paths,2 each of us has experienced countless such births; For serious and serious crimes, each type has been committed countless times. If we only repent of the sins of this life without thinking about the past, wouldn't it be like killing the grass and leaving behind the roots?

NOTE 1

Four ways of birth (four births): including fetogenesis (born from the fetus), ovum birth (born from the egg), low birth (born from humid environmental conditions) and biochemistry (born from transformation). All living beings are born in one of these four ways.

NOTE 2

Six paths, or six paths (six paths): includes all realms of heaven (heaven), human realm (human), asura realm, hell, hungry ghosts and animals.

Question: When it comes to the karma of good and evil retribution, father and son cannot bear it for each other. Now, I'm afraid I haven't finished repenting for my own sins. Isn't it an exaggeration to repent for all sentient beings?

Answer: Only seeking benefits for oneself without thinking about the benefits for others is the viewpoint of ordinary people. Having not yet been liberated, thinking about saving others is the Bodhisattva's mind. King Vu [thought that in the world] there are people who are drowning like he is drowning, there are people who are hungry and miserable like he is starving.3 Confucius [once stated his wish is] that all over the world, the old people can live happily, the young people can be nurtured

NOTE 3

Excerpted from the book Mencius, Thien Ly Lau summer.

ambition.1 Pham Trong Yem [in Nhac Duong Lau Ky wrote:] "When you need to worry, worry before people, when happy, be happy after people."

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Analects.

Question: So, lust is truly the source of birth and death, it cannot be eliminated. However, the dharma of the world is to prepare for the next life, so waiting until old age to take care of spiritual practice is not too late.

Answer: About life in general, if you take care of it early, you will do well, if you leave it late, it will be ruined. If we wait until we are old to begin practicing, it is like plowing the fields when we are hungry and digging wells when we are thirsty. What's more, there aren't many people who can live to old age. Everyone in the world is busy and busy until they are old and weak, how many people can soon let go of worldly affairs and focus on practicing before death?

Question: Living beings in the Dharma-Ending Age are extremely poor and needy, while in Buddha lands, the palaces and attics are all made of seven beautiful and solemn treasures. Why is there such an extreme difference? What's more, the Buddha always considered all sentient beings equal as his only child, so why didn't he divide his grace throughout the ten directions, so that all sentient beings could enjoy the same pleasure?

Answer: Suffering and happiness are as different as heaven and earth, that is the result in the present, but creating that present effect is

due to past causes. In that past cause, all sentient beings created the karma of killing, only the Bodhisattva practiced compassion; All sentient beings are passionate about lust, only Bodhisattvas practice pure conduct; All sentient beings are greedy and stingy, only Bodhisattvas love to give alms. Good and evil deeds are worlds apart, no one can do them for each other, then the consequences are worlds apart, no one can bear them for each other. For example, King Shun's two eyes were both bright, compared to seeing clearly, he had more than enough. [King Shun's father] Co Tau was blind, even if he had only one eye, he was lacking. Although King Thuan is a very filial person, can he take away one eye and share it with his father?

Question: The simple mud-walled thatched house shows the love of Nghieu and Thuan for the people; Building a golden palace and jade palace is the evil luxury of Kiet and Tru. The Buddha viewed the three realms as prisons, so why did he need to use the seven treasures to adorn the realms?

Answer: One side is sucking the blood of all people to build luxury buildings, the other side is the good fruit of three generations' blessings. Comparing these two things to each other, they really cannot be considered the same.

Question: The Buddha's realm is solemn and pure, of course it is ten times superior to the world, but according to the description in the sutras, I am afraid there is an excess. If you believe it all the time, wouldn't it be a myth?

Answer: What people believe is only [within the scope] of what the eyes see and the mind thinks. Places that the eye cannot see are quickly considered myths, let alone

things that the mind cannot imagine? For example, an earthworm, which only knows how to eat mud within a meter of land, takes it for fun. Who knows that there is a green dragon tumbling in the ocean, struggling to kick on the waves? Like a scarab beetle that only knows the joy of wandering around in a pile of filth, where does it know the wings of a bird flying thousands of miles away, riding the clouds and surfing the wind?

IMPLIED Tathagata1

NOTE 1

This section has 7 question and answer sections. (Author's note)

Question: Worldly people are born from the mother's door, Bodhisattvas are born from the right hip, why is that?

Answer: Mortals have many desires so they are born from the mother's door, Bodhisattvas have no desires so they are born from the right hip.

Question: Among the three realms, the most noble is the God, but to say that when the Tathagata was born, there were the Four Heavenly Kings, the Heavenly Sons of the Dao-loi heaven, all respectfully coming to serve them, is that overstating the matter?

Answer: In the sutra, the six paths of reincarnation are mentioned, and the gods are just one of them. that.2 People in the world think that there is no one more noble than the gods, but to the Buddha, the gods are nothing more than mortal beings who have not yet escaped birth and death.

NOTE 2

The six paths of reincarnation include the gods: 1. Heaven, 2. Human realm, 3. Asura realm, 4. Hell, 5. Hungry ghosts, 6. Animals.

Therefore, every time the Tathagata preaches the Dharma, there are countless numbers. The heavenly kings and Indra came together to respectfully worship and receive the revelation of the mysterious meanings.

Here I would like to briefly mention just a few things, as recorded in the Avatamsaka Sutra: "At that time, the Heavenly King from afar saw the Tathagata appear, immediately used his divine power to manifest a precious lotus flower with a lion throne, hundreds of thousands of stories high to adorn it, and hundreds of thousands of heavenly kings all respectfully bowed."

The Prajnaparamita Sutra1 says: “All over the world The world, the gods, humans, and asuras should all make offerings to [the Buddha].”

NOTE 1

The Prajnaparamita Sutra, the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra (大般若波羅蜜多 經), a total of 600 volumes, was translated by Huyen Trang Chinese language, is classified in the Great Canon of Volume 5, sutra number 220.

The Great Bao Tich Sutra2 says: "The gods in the Four Heavenly Kings heaven, the Dao-loi heaven, all scatter flowers in the sky to make offerings to the Tathagata."

NOTE 2

The Great Treasure Tich Sutra (大寶積經), a total of 120 volumes, written by him. Translated into Chinese by the Bodhi-lutika, it is included in the Mahayana Canon of Volume 11, Sutra No. 310.

The Lotus Face Sutra3 says: “The Heavenly King Indra saw the World-Honored One, immediately set up a high throne [invited the Buddha to sit], and then prostrated himself at the Buddha's feet.”

NOTE LIKE 3

The Lotus Face Sutra (蓮華面經), 2 volumes, translated into Chinese by Venerable Na-lian-de-da-xa, is included in the Mahayana Canon of Volume 12, sutra number 386.

Question: The Jade Emperor Sutra says: "The Heavenly Emperor preached the Dharma, and the Buddha came to listen and accept it." Is that not true?

Answer: The Tathagata's sutras were proclaimed by the Buddha himself and compiled by Ananda, not even a single word is false. That "Jade Emperor" Sutra was not written by the Jade Emperor himself [not yet worthy of belief], and even though he had the desire to worship the Jade Emperor, he did not know who was the most noble person. Have you never heard the Buddha teach about the noblest virtue? [Buddha taught that:] If you add up all the merits of those with the highest merits in the human world, they are not equal to a celestial being in the Four Kings heaven. If you add up all the merits and virtues of those with the highest merits in the Four Kings heaven, they are still not equal to a celestial being in the Dao Loi heaven. The Jade Emperor is the Heavenly King in the Dao Loi heaven. From the Dao Loi heaven upwards, each higher heaven [the merit] becomes more and more superior, passing through four higher heavens like that, up to the Heaven of Tha Hoa Tu Tu, still belonging to the realm of Desire. From the heavens, Tha Hoa Hoa Tu Tu ascended high.

Furthermore, each higher heaven [the merit] becomes more and more superior, going through eighteen higher heavens like that, up to the Heaven of Ultimate Form, which belongs to the world of Form. From the heaven of Ultimate Form, we go higher, with each higher heaven [the merit] becomes more and more outstanding, passing through four higher heavens like that, up to the heaven of Non-Perception, belonging to the Formless realm. Even if they reach that heaven, all the gods are still ordinary people who have not yet left samsara.

Considering again, among the saints in this world, there are the Hinayana Shravaka saints, from the sainthood of Sotapanna up to the sainthood of Arhat, a total of four levels.1 Considering the higher levels, there are the Pratyekabuddhas and Solitary Enlightened Ones. Looking even higher, that is, the positions of the Bodhisattva, there are Ten Faiths, Ten Abodes, Ten Virtues, Ten Dedications, etc., including many levels, each level has ten statuses. If you go higher, you will enter the Bodhisattva First Stage, which is the Land of Joy, gradually ascending to the Dharma Cloud Stage, again experiencing a difference of ten steps. Only then can one reach the level of Enlightenment, and then attain the First Birth, and that is on the verge of becoming a Buddha. The Buddha is called the Supreme Dharma King, because no one can be more noble. How could it be that the Jade Emperor preached the Dharma and the Buddha came to listen and accept it? Great Master Lien Tri in the Chanh Hoa Tap discusses this issue in very detail and clearly.

OF THE AM PROVINCE SHAMAN 1

NOTE 1

PREFACE

The Buddha taught only the method of contemplation of impurity for sentient beings with many desires. Practicing this contemplation method for a long time and becoming mature, naturally eliminates desire, can overcome the river of attachment, transcends the cycle of birth and death.

In my free time, I read the treatise Great Wisdom,2 borrowed the idea from it to create this chant, used to remind myself to wake up, and also to remind people to wake up.

NOTE 3

(Author's note) In the original work, all the verses in this section are written in a five-word four-literate form. When translating in Vietnamese, we changed to using seven-word quatrains to be able to convey the entire poetic meaning.

No matter how many loves will end,
How long can this body be examined carefully?

Contemplation of bloated corpses

Will one be able to escape birth and death in the future?

Blue-purple bruises and blood are leaking everywhere,
Look closely at that body,

The sight of a corpse being pierced by animals tear

Three inches stopped slightly, both humans and animals,

Contemplation of disintegrated corpses

White Bones Restaurant

Death contemplation - second time

My loved one has now said goodbye,
The eyes can't bear to look at it, the heart is filled with sadness.
The consciousness has just left the body,
The body has entered the coffin and locked it tightly.

Late at night, the house is empty and the lights are flickering,
The autumn wind is blowing coldly.
I advise anyone who is still alive,
Quiet your mind soon, meditate on the moment of death.

Contemplate the bloated corpse - second time

A cold breath arose from the body,
The corpse suddenly swelled up.
The body was swollen like a water bag,
The stomach was like a wilted melon, it was terrifying to see.

Water leaked from the dirty bag,

Being lost for so many years hates me.

The dry skin fell into pieces,

The ears and nose are now hollow,

Contemplating a decayed corpse - second time

Dry ropes accidentally tangle hair,

Message to those who are passionate about shapes and colors,

Contemplating dead bodies with blood stinky stasis - second time

Mixed in the weeds,

THE MEDITATION OF THE ORIGIN OF

AM PROVINCE MAGICIAN1

NOTE 1

Includes a preface. (Author's note)

FOREWORD

When he was about to enter Nirvana, the Buddha told the monks in the future to rely on the practice of contemplating the Four Foundations of Mindfulness to practice abiding, and they will be like Buddha.

Today is the end of the Dharma, people who practice mindfulness are very Very few, looking back at this method, I don't see anyone practicing it. Not only do I not understand the meaning, but I'm afraid that not many people even know the name of this method. How sad!

While in the middle of the mountains and forests, I was safe and sound, I read the Di Teaching chapter in the Mahaparinirvana Sutra, immediately borrowed the idea from it and used rhyme to create these chants, helping those who recite and recite the chants to increase mindfulness and eliminate delusion.

If you put these words near your seat, you will be able to wake yourself up every day, and at the same time, not forget the Buddha's admonitions.

Contemplating the impure body

A crazy thought has just arisen,
The illusory body has appeared. then.
A bundle filled with blood and pus,
Inside, outside, top and bottom, it smells foul.

The skin is like thin paper covering flesh and blood,
Ties and tendons hold only the bones.
Fur grows on the body like weeds,
Insects everywhere.

The heart, liver, lungs are all filthy,
The bright green clothes are only covered.
The four elements are inherently illusory,
The six senses are not really clear enough.

Speaking is made possible by the wind,
Movement is all made by air. twist and turn.
Forced division between men and women,
Fake names treat the main and the bare.

Three meters of mound, a hundred years to end,
A grave, eternally consecrated.
The noble and the lowly will also be let go empty-handed,
